messages:
incident-bot: Pager — P0: High error rate on redwood-inference-prod (infer-prod-7). Symptoms: multiple container OOMs, CUDA driver resets, and heavy packet drops on InfiniBand fabric. Paging oncall-sre. Runbook: /runbooks/serve-network-failure. @oncall-sre please ack :rotating_light:

alexa: acked. I'm seeing a spike in 500s from the distributed serving pool. Logs show repeated `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS` then containers dying. Kernel logs reference mlx5 and TX queue timeouts.

samir: copying kernel excerpt, might be IB-related:
```
[ 12345.678901] mlx5_core 0000:3b:00.1: mlx5e: probe failure, aborting
[ 12345.679012] mlx5_core 0000:3b:00.1: transmit queue 3 timed out
[ 12345.679123] gdr: gdr_evict: device reset detected
[ 12345.680000] WARNING: CPU: 1 PID: 2345 at nv_peer_mem.c:...
```

mike: noticed a pattern — when IB drops ~1-2% of packets burst, the latency spikes and KV cache replication stalls, leading to large queue growth on the serving side and then CUDA OOMs when the batcher accumulates too many inflight requests.

tara: quick mitigation plan: 1) throttle incoming traffic to infer-prod-7 (route ~70% to infer-prod-3/5), 2) scale down distributed replicas on rack-7, 3) enable CPU-only fallback for the heavy model to reduce GPU pressure. Who can change routing?

jordan: I can handle routing. Moving 70% traffic now via traffic-router: `kroutectl set-weight pool:infer-prod-7 30` -> `ok`  :white_check_mark:

alexa: starting node-level remediation. I'll cordon the worst nodes and drain them gradually. Commands: `kubectl cordon node/infer-7a && kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data node/infer-7a`

infra-bot: Auto-detected 3 container restarts on node infer-7a in the last 2m. Recommended: restart kernel drivers and check firmware.

samir: running quick fabric checks: `ibstat` shows port 1 state Active, but counters: `port_xmit_discards` is non-zero and `port_rcv_errors` increased rapidly. Running `ibv_devinfo -v` shows driver mismatch on node 7a.

mike: while nodes are drained, enable fallback path in runtime config to avoid multi-node KV sync:
```json
{"model_routing": "local-first", "kvcache_replication": "disabled", "batching_max_inflight": 8}
```
I'll push that as a hotfix to the config service.

tara: pushing CPU-fallback policy now. Service reports `config-update accepted`.

alexa: driver restart attempt on infer-7a: `systemctl restart rdma`; also reloaded mlx5 driver. dmesg now shows fewer tx timeouts but still seeing residual `gdr: evict` messages.

jordan: after cordon+drain, one node went healthy after a driver reload and kubelet restart. Reinstated 20% traffic to the pool to monitor.

incident-bot: Severity remains P1 while mitigation in progress. Notifying customer success for potential impact window: ~3-5m of degraded latency for some customers.

samir: I ran a targeted iperf between racks — short bursts show intermittent 0.5-1% packet loss on the PCIe->IB path. Looks like firmware-level RX ring congestion during TX bursts. Scheduling firmware rollback for NIC vendor version 4.2.1 -> 4.1.8 on affected nodes.

mike: while firmware change is scheduled, recommend keeping `batching_max_inflight` low and routing more traffic off the affected rack. Also temporarily disable kvcache replication to break the cross-node pressure cycle.

alexa: rolling driver+firmware plan: take one node, drain, apply firmware, reboot, smoke-test; if green, roll to next. ETA per node ~10min. I'm starting with infer-7b.

jordan: pre-approved by infra, proceed. I'll queue the nodes and update the incident doc with node list.

oncall-sre: taking over the thread for the next 30m. Thanks team — keep the mitigation notes in this thread. I'll escalate if any node fails the post-firmware smoke tests.

incident-bot: Handoff: oncall-sre is now primary. Next update expected by 2334568020. Please ping `#incidents` if customer impact widens. :bell:

mike: quick health check: Errors dropped from 22%->6% after traffic shift + config changes. CUDA OOM frequency halved. Still seeing occasional container restarts tied to remaining nodes awaiting firmware.

tara: customer-impact note: CS informed — some real-time endpoints may have degraded tail latencies; non-real-time batch jobs unaffected.

samir: initiated firmware rollback on infer-7b now. Monitoring NIC stats.

alexa: confirm: after firmware rollback on infer-7b and kubelet restart, node passed smoke tests (model inference sanity + kv-sync). Reintroducing node to pool at 10% traffic.

oncall-sre: last check — traffic rebalanced, config hotfix holding, firmware rollouts in progress. Marking mitigation state: partial-recovery. Will keep thread open until full roll.

incident-bot: last_message: status updated to partial-recovery. Incident channel will remain open until `full-recovery`.
